defects_fixed.title: An unreadable clang-tidy run scored as a clean scan
defects_fixed.mechanism: parsers._clang_tidy read only out/clang_tidy.err and reported findings=0 whenever its output was not there or not matchable. findings=0 is MeasurementStatus.MEASURED, not MISSING, so every clang-tidy-fed profile item scored full marks. A candidate whose source merely broke the analyzer outranked one that was genuinely clean.
defects_fixed.fix: Read both captured streams; raise ValueError when a successful run produced no readable diagnostic, which the existing _guard converts to _missing (MISSING).
defects_fixed.pre_fix_behaviour: FAILED with MeasurementStatus.MEASURED (observed by reverting the fix and re-running)

defects_fixed.title: clang-tidy diagnostics on stdout were silently dropped
defects_fixed.mechanism: Only one of the two captured streams was parsed; a build writing diagnostics to stdout produced zero findings and still reported a clean scan.
defects_fixed.fix: Concatenate out/clang_tidy.out and out/clang_tidy.err, matching the C plugin's convention.
defects_fixed.pre_fix_behaviour: FAILED (0 findings for the stdout-carried diagnostic)

defects_fixed.title: UBSan reports not at offset 0 were never recorded
defects_fixed.mechanism: _UBSAN_LINE lacked re.MULTILINE, so `^` could only match at the start of the text; finditer over a whole sanitizer report returned nothing and the run was classified clean.
defects_fixed.fix: Add re.MULTILINE and anchor the path group to the line start so it cannot absorb preceding text.
defects_fixed.verification: diagnostic_locations() on a report with a preamble line returns [('undefined-behaviour', 'src/top_words.cpp', 12, 5)]; before the fix it returned []

defects_fixed.title: Indented clang diagnostics were unparseable
defects_fixed.mechanism: _DIAGNOSTIC matched only at column 0, so an indented or prefixed diagnostic line was dropped and read as a clean run.
defects_fixed.fix: Allow leading whitespace; over-matching is contained by the caller's in-scope file filter.

defects_fixed.title: C++ quality profile was never scored by the shared evaluator
defects_fixed.mechanism: evaluator.py resolved the profile via getattr(plugin, 'python_profile', None) or getattr(plugin, 'rust_profile', None). Every other plugin publishes language_profile under the shared LanguageProfileEvaluator protocol, so for C, C++, Go and Java the profile was None: findings reached the scorer but no profile item was ever scored.
defects_fixed.fix: Read the protocol attribute language_profile. All six plugins publish it; Python and Rust retain their existing per-language accessors as aliases.
defects_fixed.regression_evidence: tests/test_cpp_plugin.py, tests/test_python_plugin.py, tests/test_rust_plugin.py, tests/test_evaluator.py, tests/test_language_extension_audit.py: 148 passed after the change

defects_fixed.title: Four C++ (and four C) fixtures could not validate against the shared schema
defects_fixed.mechanism: FixtureExpectation rejected expected_lane_findings and expected_failure values candidate_crash/build_error, so the ownership-defective, leak-defective, race-defective and exception-defective C++ fixtures (and four C fixtures) declared expectations the manifest loader refused.
defects_fixed.fix: Extend the shared schema with the two outcomes an instrumented language genuinely has. All six languages' fixture manifests now validate.

defects_fixed.title: Fixtures declaring lane findings were never analyzed
defects_fixed.mechanism: SuiteAdmission analyzed only fixtures whose variant was reference or quality_defective. The ownership/leak/race fixtures are variant faulty, so no analyzer ever ran on them and their declared expectations could not have been checked.
defects_fixed.fix: Analyze any fixture that declares expected_lane_findings; add gates instrumented-lane-defect-detected and crash-and-build-fixtures-rejected.
defects_fixed.verification_status: implemented and lint/type clean; the gates are NOT executed in this prompt because task admission requires Docker images that were not built here

defects_fixed.title: quality-defective declared scanner rule names where the gate compares families
defects_fixed.mechanism: expected_issue_families is compared by SuiteAdmission._families() against the family component of each observation's issue_key (cc.<family>.<hash>). The manifest listed scanner rule names (raw-owning-pointer, pass-by-value-container, redundant-container-copy, index-loop-container, throw-in-destructor), so the pre-existing quality-defect-detected gate could never have matched them and the fixture would have failed on names rather than on behaviour.
defects_fixed.fix: Declare the four real equivalence families: manual-ownership, value-copy, index-loop, throwing-destructor. The five rule names collapse to four families because pass-by-value-container and redundant-container-copy share value-copy, which is exactly the single-penalty behaviour PCB-21-3 requires.
defects_fixed.verification: Ran the real context scanner over admission/quality-defective/src/top_words.cpp: the violation families are exactly {index-loop, manual-ownership, throwing-destructor, value-copy}, matching the declaration.

defects_fixed.title: C++ lane declarations named families no observation can carry
defects_fixed.mechanism: The manifest declared asan: [double-free, heap-use-after-free] and asan: [resource-leak], but the profile resolves those checks to the equivalence families manual-ownership and undefined-behaviour. Had the new gate run, every lane fixture would have failed on names rather than on behaviour.
defects_fixed.fix: Declare the profile's real equivalence families.

verified_by_inspection_not_defect.finding: Release and sanitizer profiles are separated by construction: the sanitizer lane resolves through lock.profile_for() and the performance lane through lock.release_profile(), and every compile lane resolves flags through the single cxxflags() choke point.
verified_by_inspection_not_defect.evidence: The serialized performance plan contains no '-fsanitize' token; warmup_iterations=5 and measured_iterations=20 are frozen and do not vary per candidate.

verified_by_inspection_not_defect.finding: Incompatible instrumentation is rejected at the lock, and the release and sanitizer profiles are disjoint.
verified_by_inspection_not_defect.evidence: lock.check_sanitizers(('address','thread')) and (('undefined','thread')) both raise LockError; ('address','undefined') is accepted because they share one build profile. lock.release_profile().cxxflags == ('-O3','-DNDEBUG','-fno-omit-frame-pointer'); lock.profile_for(('address',)).cxxflags == ('-g','-O1','-fno-omit-frame-pointer','-fsanitize=address,undefined','-fno-sanitize-recover=all').

verified_by_inspection_not_defect.finding: A non-owning raw pointer produces no finding at all.
verified_by_inspection_not_defect.evidence: Running the real context scanner over `void f(const std::string*); int g(const char*);` yields no raw-pointer finding; raw_pointer_nonowning emits verdict=benign_in_context, which parsers maps to NOT_APPLICABLE and observations nulls out.

verified_by_inspection_not_defect.finding: The single-sanitizer-plan `break` in analysis_plans is correct, not a defect: ASan and ThreadSanitizer are declared incompatible and cannot share a process, so at most one instrumented lane may be built for a task.
verified_by_inspection_not_defect.evidence: config/languages/cpp-toolchain-v1.json incompatible_instrumentation lists [address, thread] and [undefined, thread]; taskspec.SANITIZER_REQUIREMENTS maps asan -> (address, undefined) because they share one build profile and runtime.

verified_by_inspection_not_defect.finding: UBSan needs no separate parser entry: it shares the asan build profile and runtime, and cpp.ubsan.candidate-defect shares the undefined-behaviour equivalence family with cpp.asan.candidate-defect, so it collapses to one issue. A 'ubsan' key in PARSERS would have been unreachable dead code because 'ubsan' is not in KNOWN_ANALYZERS.
No double-penalty defect found. One construct reported by several tools collapses to one scored issue through equivalence families, and a non-owning raw pointer is not a failure.
verified_by_inspection_not_defect.evidence: tests/test_cpp_profile.py: a non-owning const T* / const char* produces no finding; a duplicated report of one rule at one site cannot change a score; several benign non-owning-pointer findings leave the score at 10000.
